name: Chewing gum for face fat
lead: Chewing gum for face fat is a practice, found in appearance-focused online communities, of chewing gum for long stretches to slim the cheeks and sharpen the jawline. Practitioners say the repeated jaw work burns fat over the cheeks and jaw or builds the chewing muscles, so that the lower face looks leaner and more defined.[3][4]

The idea belongs to the family of facial-slimming ideas built on spot reduction, the principle that exercising one muscle group reduces fat in the area around it. Encyclopedic sources describe spot reduction and report exercise studies finding that fat is lost from the whole body through diet and overall energy balance rather than from the exercised site.[1] A T Nation forum poster in 2002 made the same point in lay terms: chewing lots of gum does not make the face 'ripped'.[5]

No published human trial found has tested chewing gum for facial fat.[2] Chewing gum has been studied for other outcomes, including short-term memory, dental plaque and recovery of bowel function after abdominal surgery.[2]

paras: Proponents of the practice say that extended chewing works the jaw and cheek muscles and thereby thins the face or sharpens the jawline. Variations include chewing for long sessions each day and using hard or mastic-style gums.
The practice is closely related to jaw-exerciser devices and to arguments about masseter size, but this article concerns gum itself.

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and fitness communities
paras: A 2003 T Nation thread on training jaw muscles included a poster saying everyone he knew with strong jaw muscles chewed gum constantly, and adding that low body fat helps because the face loses fat quickly and features show more.[3] A 2002 thread on spot reduction included a reply that targeted muscle work does not reduce fat locally, citing chewing gum and the face as an example.[5] A T Nation article on eating habits, titled 'Strong Jaw, Lean Body', discusses how eating speed and chewing relate to the face and appetite.[4]

Many in these communities distinguish two effects: muscle growth in the jaw, which they argue could add width and definition, and fat loss over the cheeks, which they attribute mainly to lowering overall body fat.

Spot reduction is described as a claim that physiologists and fitness professionals regard as unsupported by research. In a six-week trial of 24 sedentary adults cited in the encyclopedic literature, a group performing abdominal exercises five days a week did not lose subcutaneous abdominal fat, although core endurance improved.[1] A study of tennis players cited there found larger muscles in the dominant forearm but no difference in skinfold fat between arms.[1]

The same source states that fat distribution is strongly influenced by genetics and that fat is lost from the body as a whole through diet and regular exercise.[1] These findings concern the trunk and limbs; the sources reviewed here do not report trials of facial fat in particular.

sections.h: Other documented effects of chewing gum
paras: A 2011 review found that chewing gum before cognitive testing was associated with better working and episodic memory for roughly 15 to 20 minutes.[2] Sugar-free gum sweetened with xylitol has been shown to reduce cavities and plaque, and the American Dental Association recommends chewing sugar-free gum for 20 minutes after meals.[2] Randomized studies and a 2008 meta-analysis reported faster bowel recovery after colectomy in patients who chewed gum.[2]

Gum containing sorbitol in large amounts may cause gas or diarrhea, and a 2025 study reported that gum releases micro- and nanoplastics into saliva; the health effects of this are under investigation.[2] None of these outcomes concern facial appearance.

No studies found. No published trial in the sources reviewed has measured changes in facial fat after gum chewing. Related research on spot reduction in the abdomen and forearm is summarised above.[1]

lore.intro: Chewing is discussed in strength-training and appearance forums as a way to build the jaw and lean the face, with other posters pointing to overall body fat as the main driver.[3][5]

claims.claim: Chewing gum all day builds a stronger, more defined jaw
claims.believers: A poster in a jaw-training thread said people with strong jaw muscles chew gum incessantly.[3]
claims.experts: No published trial in the sources has measured jaw muscle size or facial shape after gum chewing.

claims.claim: Chewing gum burns fat from the cheeks
claims.believers: Proponents say working the facial muscles slims the face.[3]
claims.experts: Spot reduction studies cited in encyclopedic sources report no selective fat loss at the exercised site; fat is lost from the whole body.[1]

claims.claim: A lean face comes from low overall body fat
claims.believers: Forum posters say that a low body fat percentage makes the face lose fat quickly and features show more.[3]
claims.experts: Encyclopedic sources state that fat is lost from the body as a whole through diet and exercise, with distribution strongly influenced by genetics.[1]

card.summary: The idea that chewing gum melts cheek fat; it rests on spot reduction, which exercise research does not support, and no trial tests it.
card.note: No study has tested gum for facial fat; spot reduction is not supported by exercise research.

quick.overview:
Some looksmaxxing circles say that chewing gum for long stretches slims the cheeks and sharpens the jawline by burning facial fat.

The idea is a version of spot reduction. Exercise research cited in encyclopedic sources reports that working a muscle does not selectively reduce the fat above it, and no trial has examined gum and facial fat.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say repeated chewing works the jaw and cheek muscles and burns local fat. Physiologists cited in the literature say fat is lost from the whole body through overall energy balance, with distribution largely set by genetics.
quick.risks: Gum is generally regarded as low risk. Sorbitol-sweetened gum in large amounts may cause gas or diarrhea. No studies found on facial-fat effects.

chain: Prolonged chewing works the masseter and cheek muscles
Practitioners expect local fat loss and stronger jaw muscles
Lower face looks leaner and more defined
angle.text: People chew gum for extended sessions hoping to slim the cheeks and bring out the jaw. Forum users also link low body fat to a more visible jaw, and pair chewing with overall leaning out.
